chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, concerning

regarding a man who goes out to Najd for some need. He said: He may enter Makkah without ihram. The correct way to understand this report is that we interpret it as applying to one who went out and returned within that same month, for ihram is not required of him. But as for one who enters it initially, or returns to it after the end of the month, then ihram is obligatory upon him. This detail is indicated by the evidence.

key_terms.التَّفْصِيلِ: the legal distinction or detailed differentiation in the ruling
key_terms.الْإِحْرَامَ: the state of consecration required for pilgrimage-related entry
key_terms.الْحَاجَةِ: a need or purpose for which one travels
key_terms.بِغَيْرِ إِحْرَامٍ: without entering the state of ihram
key_terms.ذَلِكَ الشَّهْرِ: that same month in which the person had exited
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Makkah, the sacred city being entered
key_terms.نَجْدٍ: Najd, the region to which the man travels for a need

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to enter Makkah without ihram according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal ruling on entering Makkah without ihram. It explains that the permission applies to someone who left and returned within the same month, whereas one entering afresh or returning after the month has ended must enter in ihram.
